skills.name: Prove triangles congruent: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS

note.text:
Two triangles are congruent if any one of these is true:
• SSS: the three sides of one equal the three sides of the other.
• SAS: two sides and the included angle (the angle between them) are equal.
• ASA (or AAS): two angles and a corresponding side are equal.
• RHS: both have a right angle, equal hypotenuses and one other equal side.
AAA is not a test (it only shows similarity), and SSA (angle not between the sides) is not a test.

sections.heading: You do not need everything
sections.text:
To show two triangles are congruent, you do not need all six measurements to match. Some sets of three are enough to fix the triangle completely.
If you know three sides, there is only one triangle you can draw with them. That gives the first test, SSS.

sections.heading: The four tests
sections.text:
• SSS: three pairs of equal sides.
• SAS: two pairs of equal sides and the angle between them (the included angle).
• ASA: two pairs of equal angles and a pair of corresponding sides.
• RHS: a right angle, equal hypotenuses and one more pair of equal sides.
In a proof, give a reason for each equal part: "given", "common side", "vertically opposite angles", "opposite sides of a parallelogram"…

sections.heading: Two that do not work
sections.text:
AAA: triangles with the same three angles have the same shape but can be different sizes. They are similar, not necessarily congruent.
SSA: two sides and an angle that is not between them. Sometimes two different triangles fit, so it proves nothing. The exception is RHS, where the angle is a right angle.

key_words.meaning: the angle between two given sides
a side shared by both triangles
a chain of facts, each with a reason, leading to the result

examples: AB = DE, BC = EF, CA = FD → SSS
angle A = angle D, AB = DE, angle B = angle E → ASA

mistake.wrong: Equal angles, so the triangles are congruent (AAA)
mistake.right: Equal angles only show the triangles are similar
mistake.why: AAA does not fix the size. You need at least one pair of equal sides too.

worked_example.problem: ABCD is a parallelogram with diagonal AC. Show that ΔABC ≅ ΔCDA.
steps: AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal).
AC is common to both triangles.

cards.idea: SSS: three pairs of equal sides.
SAS needs the included angle: the angle between the two sides.
example: The angle between AB and BC is angle B.

pick.q: In ΔPQR, which angle is included between sides PQ and QR?
e: Angle P is between PQ and PR.
Angle R is between PR and QR.
Two sides always meet at an angle.
pick.y: PQ and QR meet at Q.

pick.q: In ΔABC, which angle is included between sides CA and AB?
e: Angle B is between AB and BC.
Angle C is between BC and CA.
Angle ABC is angle B.
pick.y: CA and AB meet at A.

pick.q: In ΔXYZ, which angle is included between sides YZ and ZX?
e: Angle X is between XY and XZ.
Angle Y is between XY and YZ.
Angle XYZ is angle Y.
pick.y: YZ and ZX meet at Z.

cards.idea: AAA and SSA are not tests of congruence.
example: Equal angles alone give similar triangles, which can differ in size.

pick.q: All three sides of one triangle equal the three sides of the other.
e: SAS needs an angle.
RHS needs a right angle.
AAA is not a congruence test.

pick.q: Two sides and the angle between them are equal.
e: Only two sides are known.
Only one side is known in ASA.
SSA is not a test; here the angle is between the sides.
pick.y: Two sides and the included angle: SAS.

pick.q: Two angles and the side between them are equal.
e: Only one side is known.
Only one side is known.
A side is known too: that makes it ASA.
pick.y: Two angles and a side: ASA.

pick.q: Both are right-angled, the hypotenuses are equal and one other pair of sides is equal.
e: The right angle is not between the two given sides.
Only two pairs of sides are given.
Only one angle (the right angle) is given.

questions.prompt: {X.q} Which condition proves the triangles congruent?

pick.q: Which of these is NOT a test for congruent triangles?
e: SSS is a test.
SAS is a test.
RHS is a test.
pick.y: Equal angles only show the triangles are similar; they can be different sizes.

pick.q: Which of these is NOT a test for congruent triangles?
e: ASA is a test.
SSS is a test.
SAS with the included angle is a test.
pick.y: With the angle not between the two sides, two different triangles can be drawn.

pick.q: Two triangles have equal angles of 40°, 60° and 80°. Are they congruent?
w: No, they cannot be similar either
e: AAA is not a congruence test.
ASA needs a pair of equal sides as well.
Equal angles make them similar.
pick.y: Equal angles give the same shape, not necessarily the same size.

pick.q: In ΔPQR, which angle is included between sides PQ and QR?
e: Angle P is between PQ and PR.
Angle R is between PR and QR.
Two sides always meet at an angle.
pick.y: PQ and QR meet at Q.

pick.q: In ΔABC, which angle is included between sides CA and AB?
e: Angle B is between AB and BC.
Angle C is between BC and CA.
Angle ABC is angle B.
pick.y: CA and AB meet at A.

pick.q: In ΔXYZ, which angle is included between sides YZ and ZX?
e: Angle X is between XY and XZ.
Angle Y is between XY and YZ.
Angle XYZ is angle Y.
pick.y: YZ and ZX meet at Z.

pick.q: In ΔABC and ΔDEF: AB = DE, angle B = angle E and BC = EF. Which test shows they are congruent?
e: Only two sides are given.
Only one angle is given.
Angle B is between AB and BC: SAS applies.
pick.y: Two sides and the included angle.

pick.q: In ΔPQR and ΔXYZ: angle P = angle X, PQ = XY, angle Q = angle Y. Which test applies?
e: Two angles and one side are given, not two sides.
A side is also given, so it is ASA.
No right angle is given.
pick.y: Two angles and the side between them.

pick.q: The diagonal AC of a kite ABCD (AB = AD, CB = CD) splits it into two triangles. Which test shows ΔABC ≅ ΔADC?
e: No angle is known to be equal yet.
No right angle is given.
No angles are given.
pick.y: AB = AD, CB = CD and AC is common: SSS.

pick.q: O is the midpoint of AB and of CD. Why are ΔAOC and ΔBOD congruent?
pick.r: SAS: OA = OB, angle AOC = angle BOD (vertically opposite), OC = OD
e: AC = BD is not given.
AAA is not a test.
Nothing says the angles are right angles.
pick.y: Two sides from the midpoints and the vertically opposite angles between them.

pick.q: In an isosceles triangle ABC (AB = AC), M is the midpoint of BC. Why is ΔABM ≅ ΔACM?
pick.r: SSS: AB = AC, BM = CM, AM is common
w: SAS: AB = AC and angle B = angle C
e: The angle given is not between the given sides.
AAA is not a test.
RHS needs a right angle that is not given.

pick.q: AD is the perpendicular from A to BC in triangle ABC, and AB = AC. Why is ΔABD ≅ ΔACD?
pick.r: RHS: right angles at D, AB = AC (hypotenuses), AD common
w: SAS: AB = AC and AD common
e: The right angle is not between AB and AD.
One side and only the right angle are known.
SSA is not a test; RHS is the special case that works.
pick.y: Right angle, equal hypotenuses, a common side: RHS.
